correctness.rationale: All assertions reduce to two nonoverlapping strict comparisons of i.i.d. atomless gaps. The four joint probabilities are 0, 1/36, 1/12, 1/16, yielding covariance −1/16, −5/144, 1/48, 0 after subtracting 1/16. Exact finite variance follows by pair sums. Bounded 3-dependent blocking plus Lyapunov yields the CLT with strictly positive 5/144 variance. The package verifier enumerated every gap ranking for lag 1–4 and n=1–6, passing 28 exact-rational comparisons.

originality.rationale: The exact rank-comparison covariance and variance constants hold uniformly for every atomless i.i.d. positive gap law; the closest inspected geometric sources address marginal lengths or a distinct superhomogeneous model. Gaussian MA(1) stationary peak-count papers provide partial overlap but their accessible descriptions do not imply the universal distribution-free assertion. Historical priority is uncertain because the most relevant older peak-count full texts were unavailable.
residual_risks: Full text of Ku–Seneta (1994), the closest Gaussian MA(1) peak-count study, was unavailable; it may contain a stronger all-innovation statement not reflected in the Gaussian-specific abstract.
The full Bandt–Shiha (2007) ordinal-pattern article could contain general identities covering the rank-comparison reduction.
The 2012 Newman–Turcotte–Malamud full text could not be examined; nearest-neighbor cluster descriptions are distinct in accessible statements.
The full literature on ordinal MA(1) statistics is not exhaustively indexed; search failures do not prove priority.

value.rationale: Locally dominant Voronoi cell lengths are geometrically natural observables. The complete exact signed short-range covariance profile has a nontrivial lag-three attraction after two negative lags; the exact finite-window variance and CLT show a large, law-independent suppression of peak count noise by a factor of 5/27 compared with fictitious independent peaks. This resolves a natural local-to-global dependence statistic and is not solely a relabeling of the single-cell gamma law.
